parsed.explanation: The combined national/state regime is hostile at the border and in national custody, while the division currently has no bathroom ban or trans-identity offence. A trans visitor’s sharpest exposure is national: binary-sex passport/visa policy, secondary screening for marker discrepancy, possible refusal and non-automatic lifetime fraud finding, plus documented immigration-custody abuse. The division adds a minor care ban and pending facility/prison bills, but current state law leaves restroom use unrestricted and provides a hate-crime aggravator. Courts and local ordinances mitigate unevenly. Result: high risk, below reduced-risk tiers and above extreme-criminalisation anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport/visa rules; X markers no longer issued; document discrepancy can trigger refusal, secondary screening, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; athlete entry ban; foreign advisories and detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements with limited waivers; litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor crosses the national border with a home passport and visa; the state/province layer cannot offset national screening or visa adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Document discrepancy can escalate to immigration detention; trans men in immigration custody reportedly faced forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; national prisons adopted conversion-style policies; detentions over visa issues reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national orders have been enjoined; fraud finding is not automatic. No documented protection reaches national immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border suspicion can move the traveller into national immigration custody, where state/province protections do not operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching gender identity; many states/provinces ban such access. The division currently has no bathroom ban, but a pending bill would restrict school facilities and prison housing.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law places no current restriction on restroom use matching gender identity; two cities protect it; a court injunction bars school restriction in one case.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility restrictions reach national buildings and funded facilities; the division’s current permissive rule does not cancel the national layer.

care_services.exposure: The division bans gender-transition care for anyone under 18, covering surgery, puberty blockers and hormones; a trans visitor under 18 cannot obtain that care here. Adult availability is not documented; national insurance/funding restrictions are pending.
care_services.protection: No documented visitor-facing care protection. The state/province hate-crimes law does not address care access.
care_services.interaction: A minor traveller enters the state/province care ban; adult care access remains an open question; national rules overlay both.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders and counterterrorism strategy use “radical gender ideology” and prioritize “radically pro-transgender” groups; DOJ reward guidance and school-prosecution order create official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text says simple disagreement is not targeted; courts have blocked several orders; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat-framing raises reporting and outing risk; the division has no equivalent campaign but cannot offset national enforcement rhetoric.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 care ban; school notification law; national executive order directing prosecution of teachers who use preferred names/pronouns; pending state bill would restrict school facilities and prison housing. A trans minor visitor cannot access transition care.
minors_guardians.protection: Current state law has no bathroom ban; a court injunction protects one student’s school bathroom use; local ordinances exist in two cities.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian faces the state/province care ban and national school/entry rules; the state facility bill is not law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of trans-specific street violence against visitors in this dossier; airport security pat-downs can out travellers. Local violence rates and police response are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The state/province hate-crimes law since 2019 makes gender identity an aggravating circumstance; local anti-discrimination ordinances exist; no current state bathroom ban.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hate-crime enhancement exists, but charging practice and police response to anti-trans violence are not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key rules are in litigation; adult care access, hate-crime charging, facility-bill prospects and enforcement against visitors are unresolved; national passport restrictions took effect after a Supreme Court order.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties challenges, court injunctions, a legal-aid FAQ, local ordinances and a national hate-crimes statute provide partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate unevenly across national and state/province layers; pending outcomes can change exposure during a visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve document-marker mismatch at entry, public outing and denial or confiscation. This dossier adds national facility restrictions, possible immigration detention and documented custody abuse, so it sits below 0.35-A.
0.55-B has an administrative delay but no detention, and local guidelines resolve the case. Here refusal, possible lifetime ineligibility and custody harm remain live, so this is materially lower.

0.75-C has a care-record mismatch but a protective directive, no detention and working local recourse. This dossier lacks equivalent visitor-facing protection at the border and in custody, so it is far lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a hostile national border and custody system with a state/province that currently lacks a bathroom ban but bans transition care for minors and is moving toward restrictive facility and prison rules. For an adult visitor, the main documented harms are entry refusal, invasive screening, possible immigration detention and abuse, and national facility exclusion. For a minor travelling with a guardian, the state care ban adds a concrete care-access barrier. Local protections and hate-crime law are real but do not reach national border or custody exposures. The rating reflects high risk, not catastrophic criminalisation.
